To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) RGB-D object recognition can be improved by a late fusion of two separate CNN streams, (ii) depth data can be learned with CNNs without the need of large depth datasets, (iii) depth data can also be augmented with noise patterns for robust learning.

1) a multimodal architecture that combines RGB and depth information outperforms the single modality architectures, 2) a multi-stage training approach is essential for accurate learning, 3) an effective encoding of the depth information for CNN is essential to enable learning from small datasets and to enable learning with noisy data.

(i) RGB-D object recognition is best solved by a late fusion architecture, (ii) the proposed encoding of depth data enables CNNs to learn from limited training data and (iii) the proposed data augmentation scheme enables robust learning with depth data
In summary, our research is concerned with
two main questions: (1) How do we learn robust object recognition from noisy data? (2) How can we leverage the power of CNNs for RGB-D object recognition?

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
we present a novel architecture for RGB-D object recognition and show that our architecture is capable of robust learning with imperfect data.
our proposed method achieves the state-of-the-art performance in RGB-D object recognition in both simulated and real-world settings.
we have shown that CNNs can be effectively used for RGB-D object recognition, and that our proposed architecture is robust to noise.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we present a novel architecture for object recognition in RGB-D settings, which is robust to noise and can learn with small amounts of data.
we show the potential of deep learning for object recognition with RGB-D data and that we propose a novel architecture for robust object recognition in the presence of noise.
we present a robust RGB-D architecture for real-world object recognition that can learn from imperfect depth data and achieve state-of-the-art recognition results in challenging noisy settings.
The main takeaway from our work is that
CNNs are a powerful tool for object recognition in RGB-D images and that they are robust enough to learn with imperfect data.
the use of depth data is a key enabler of object recognition in real-world robotics settings.
CNNs, when combined with the proposed encoding of depth data and multi-stage training, can be used for learning robust object recognition in RGB-D images.
